name: Adam Todd
bio:
Adam Todd is a Professor of Pharmaceutical Public Health, and Deputy Head of the School of Pharmacy at Newcastle University. He is a qualified pharmacist registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council, and a Fellow of the Royal Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain. He was previously a Senior Lecturer at Durham University where he held the roles of MPharm Programme Director, Director of Education, and Deputy Director of the Centre of Health and Inequalities Research (CHIR). He was awarded a Readership in 2017, and a personal Chair in 2021.

His research is highly interdisciplinary, and uses methods from the social sciences, public health, clinical medicine, and epidemiology. He leads a programme of research that applies pharmaceutical knowledge to prevent disease, prolong life, promote health, and reduce health inequalities, across different populations. His research outputs have had considerable impact on policy and practice.

Adam has a number of international research collaborations across Europe, the United States and Australia. He is a member of CHAIN, the Centre of Global Health Inequalities Research – a leading international research centre that seeks to monitor, explain, and reduce inequalities in health. He is also a steering group member of the English Deprescribing Network (EDeN) – a network established to reduce inappropriate and problematic polypharmacy through deprescribing.

He has experience of serving on national research committees, and has previously contributed to the NIHR HTA Prioritisation Committee for community health and social care. Adam acts as Chair for the Scientific Advisory Panel for Pharmacy Research UK (the principal research charity supporting pharmacy to improve healthcare for the benefit of patients and the public) and the NIHR Research for Patient Benefit for Yorkshire North East.

Adam has total career research funding of over £15 million, including funding from the NIHR, Macmillan Cancer Research, the Barbour Foundation, and the Sir Bobby Robson Foundation. Adam reviews for more than 30 international peer reviewed journals, serves on a number of journal editorial boards, and has published more than 150 peer-reviewed research articles, as well as an international patent.

In addition to his research activities, Adam is also actively involved in delivering the MPharm Programme at Newcastle; he approaches pharmacy education in an integrated way, and combines both science and practice elements in his teaching. Using this integrated approach, Adam has published three international books focusing on drug metabolism, antibacterial and anticancer therapeutics. He is a Senior Fellow of the Higher Education Academy, and has previously served as academic member of the General Pharmaceutical Council Accreditation and Recognition Panel.

Adam still contributes to the care of patients on a regular basis; he works alongside the specialist palliative care Multidisciplinary Team at St. Benedict’s Hospice, providing guidance on (de)prescribing; he also regularly works as a community pharmacist delivering public health interventions to the local community.
